mbm-2176.clue: I have questions about the chipped teapot.
mbm-2176.quote: Everybody else stops at the silver service. I grew up with a pot just like the chipped one in the next case. The museum volunteer let me turn the archive photograph over. Someone had written Grandma's best.

mbm-2177.clue: I dance milonga in my kitchen socks.
mbm-2177.quote: I practice the little weight changes while the coffee perks. One morning our downstairs neighbor knocked on the ceiling in perfect time. I invited her up. We danced in our socks till the coffee was ready.

mbm-2178.clue: I tie birthday ribbons to a paddle.
mbm-2178.quote: We tied seven bright ribbons to our guide's paddle for her birthday. The first wave soaked them. At the takeout they looked like seven tiny fish hanging up to dry.

mbm-2179.clue: I tried reading a whole book upside down.
mbm-2179.quote: My nephew read across the breakfast table and I didn't want to take his book away. By the middle chapter I could almost keep up. By the last one we'd squeezed into the same chair.

mbm-2180.clue: I always play the volcano hole twice.
mbm-2180.quote: The plastic lava lights up when the ball goes in. My brother took me there the night the power failed. We played by flashlight and supplied the eruption noises ourselves.

mbm-2181.clue: I know my grandfather's tiles by their backs.
mbm-2181.quote: He carved a tiny notch in every domino after one disappeared into the neighbor's set. I inherited all twenty-eight. Face down they look like a flock of birds with one wing raised.

mbm-2182.clue: I throw a disc for the bakery crowd.
mbm-2182.quote: The alley behind the bakery is just wide enough for a pass. Bakers on break lean on the doorframe and score our throws by the quality of the wobble. Crooked flights earn applause.

mbm-2183.clue: I always take a blue enamel bowl.
mbm-2183.quote: I forgot my camping pillow and set my jacket on the upside-down bowl. Woke up with a round dent in my cheek. Now I use it strictly for breakfast.

mbm-2184.clue: I count a town's public clocks.
mbm-2184.quote: Tour brochures always show the grand clock tower. Give me the clock over the fishmonger's window. I spent six happy minutes there once watching a wooden trout jump on the hour.

mbm-2185.clue: I ski under the chairlift on purpose.
mbm-2185.quote: My little cousins like to spot my red scarf from above. One run they yelled somebody else's name the whole way down. Apparently another skier has excellent taste in scarves.

mbm-2186.clue: I keep the torn half of every ticket.
mbm-2186.quote: My favorite cinema still tears tickets at the door. After a good film I slip the stub into whichever jacket I wore. Finding one in July is like accidentally catching the second show.

mbm-2187.clue: I use the window to check my seams.
mbm-2187.quote: Hold a quilt top up to the glass and every bulky seam shows itself. My neighbor thought I'd put up stained glass. I hated to disappoint her, so I left it there till dinner.

mbm-2188.clue: I learned the river by getting quiet.
mbm-2188.quote: Our guide had us stow the chatter on one stretch and listen. I heard gravel ticking under the raft. The next wave sent cold water straight up my sleeve and I broke the silence.

mbm-2189.quote: We stop an anime at a busy background and everybody picks out the weirdest detail. I won last Thursday with a pigeon wearing an apron. We never did find out what it sold.

mbm-2190.clue: I put one pocket in every quilt.
mbm-2190.quote: My niece sleeps with her bus ticket from the first time she rode alone. I put a pocket in the binding just big enough for it. Now her quilt can keep a secret.

mbm-2191.clue: I choose the canoe seat that squeaks.
mbm-2191.quote: My father swore a dab of wax would fix it. I kept forgetting the wax. Now he's gone and I hear every bend of the creek the way I heard it sitting behind him.

mbm-2192.clue: I trade cards according to the weather.
mbm-2192.quote: On rainy market days I bring my water creatures. Someone finally traded me the little frog knight for a thunder giant. I keep him in front even though his stats are awful.

mbm-2193.clue: I read the endings to my tomato plants.
mbm-2193.quote: I can't take a good last page sitting down. I carry the book out back and read the ending out loud. The tomatoes give me time to get over it.

mbm-2194.clue: I borrowed a villain from the laundromat.
mbm-2194.quote: While my jeans spun I invented a coat thief who only stole sleeves. The woman folding towels beside me suggested a much crueler ending. The story's hers as much as mine now.

mbm-2195.clue: I mark my quilt rows with crackers.
mbm-2195.quote: I lay one cracker beside each finished strip and eat them when the row count comes out right. Last time the dog helped with the arithmetic. I had to measure the whole thing again.

mbm-2196.clue: I play son on the steps after supper.
mbm-2196.quote: Our singer insists the stairwell has better acoustics than the living room. He's right. A neighbor two floors up contributes a broom-handle beat and always comes in on time.

mbm-2197.clue: I kayak out to the old piling.
mbm-2197.quote: There's a boot balanced on the piling at the bend. It's been there through three floods. I paddle out to wish it luck whenever the river starts creeping up.

mbm-2198.clue: I made a scarf for a very short winter.
mbm-2198.quote: I was three rows in when the weather turned warm. I joined the ends and put it on my teapot. Only crochet project I've ever finished over one cup of tea.

mbm-2199.clue: I dance with the fan on high.
mbm-2199.quote: When we practice the quickstep at home, the fan lifts one edge of the rug. My partner calls it the hill. We roll the rug away before the music starts.

mbm-2200.clue: I made a quilt wide enough for the bird.
mbm-2200.quote: My friend's old parrot travels on her shoulder. Whenever she pulled her lap quilt up, the bird got left outside. I added a soft green corner he could perch on. He inspects my stitching with his beak.
